audited_plan.image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a sea lion's head and upper torso emerging from green water. The animal has dark brown, wet fur, prominent long white whiskers, and a visible external ear flap. The mouth is slightly open, revealing teeth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head profile appears relatively smooth and rounded without the distinct, bony protrusion of a sagittal crest typical of mature male sea lions. This suggests the subject may be a female or juvenile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small external ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an eared seal (Otariid) and not a true seal.
Long, thick, light-colored whiskers are highly prominent against the dark fur and water background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Fur is short and coarse ranging from brown to dark grey, lighter on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible fur is dark brown and appears sleek/wet (consistent with short/coarse texture when wet). While the ventral surface isn't fully visible, the dorsal coloration matches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The neck and shoulder area show the thick, muscular build characteristic of a large marine mammal.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Males develop thick neck mane and are significantly larger than females.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no visible thick mane of longer hair around the neck; the transition from head to body is smooth, further suggesting a female or non-dominant male.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreflippers are submerged or outside the frame; only the head and neck are clearly visible above water.
